[id="removed-features"]
= Removed features

This section lists breaking changes in {product} {product-version}.

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHBUGS-3340
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhbugs-3340", role="rn-done"]
Scorecard provider configuration moves to scorecard.metricProviders::
+
--
[IMPORTANT]
====
This is a breaking change. Scorecard provider configuration moves from `scorecard.plugins` to `scorecard.metricProviders` in the `app-config.yaml` file. You must update your Scorecard configuration to use the new structure.
====

You can configure thresholds in the application configuration for a provider (all metrics of the provider) or for individual metrics. Metric-level thresholds take precedence over provider-level thresholds.

Provider IDs now use the `<datasource>.<providerName>` format. You can configure thresholds at two levels:

. `metricProviders.<datasource>.<providerName>.thresholds` applies to all metrics that a provider provides.
. `metricProviders.<datasource>.<providerName>.metrics.<metricName>.thresholds` applies to one specific metric.

Threshold annotations must now use the full metric ID:

`scorecard.io/<metricId>.thresholds.rules.<key>`

For example:

.Old configuration
[source,yaml]
----
scorecard:
  plugins:
    github:
      openPRs:
        schedule: # ...
        thresholds: # ...
----

.New configuration
[source,yaml]
----
scorecard:
  metricProviders:
    github:
      openPRs:
        schedule: # ...
        thresholds: # ...
----

The Filecheck provider now uses the `filecheck.fileExistence` provider ID, and its file configuration moves under `options`:

[source,yaml]
----
scorecard:
  metricProviders:
    filecheck:
      fileExistence:
        options:
          files:
            license: LICENSE
            codeowners: CODEOWNERS
        thresholds: # ...
        schedule: # ...
----
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHBUGS-3956
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhbugs-3956", role="heads-up jtype-bug jstatus-review rn-done"]
Scorecard aggregation cards must be reconfigured by using `app.extensions` in the New Frontend System::
+
--
[IMPORTANT]
====
This is a breaking change. In the New Frontend System, the previous Scorecard card mount points in `dynamic-plugins.yaml` no longer work. If you configured Scorecard aggregation cards through those mount points, you must reconfigure them by using `app.extensions` in `app-config.yaml`.
====

In the New Frontend System, you configure Scorecard aggregation cards in the `app-config.yaml` application configuration file by using `app.extensions`.

For a read-only homepage, configure one or more `scorecard-aggregated-card` instances in `widgetLayout`. Set `props.aggregationId` to a Scorecard metric ID, such as `github.openPRs` or `jira.openIssues`, or to the key of an aggregation KPI that is configured in `scorecard.aggregationKPIs`.

.Read-only homepage configuration
[source,yaml]
----
app:
  extensions:
    - page:home: false
    - page:homepage:
        config:
          path: /
          title: Home
    - api:home/visits: true
    - app-root-element:home/visit-listener: true
    - home-page-layout:homepage/dynamic-homepage-layout:
        config:
          customizable: false
          widgetLayout:
            scorecard-aggregated-card:
              - id: ScorecardGithubOpenPRs
                props:
                  aggregationId: github.openPRs
                priority: 410
                breakpoints:
                  xl: { w: 4, h: 6, x: 0, y: 0 }
                  lg: { w: 4, h: 6, x: 0, y: 0 }
                  md: { w: 6, h: 6, x: 0, y: 0 }
                  sm: { w: 6, h: 6, x: 0, y: 0 }
                  xs: { w: 12, h: 6, x: 0, y: 0 }
                  xxs: { w: 12, h: 6, x: 0, y: 0 }

homepage:
  defaultWidgets:
    - id: scorecard-aggregated-card
      ref: scorecard-aggregated-card
----

For a customizable homepage, omit `widgetLayout` and set `customizable: true`. On first load, the Scorecard card shows an `Aggregation ID is required` message because no aggregation ID is configured centrally. Set the aggregation ID on the card to a metric ID, such as `github.openPRs` or `jira.openIssues`, or to a custom aggregation ID that is configured under `scorecard.aggregationKPIs`.

.Customizable homepage configuration
[source,yaml]
----
app:
  extensions:
    - page:home: false
    - page:homepage:
        config:
          path: /
          title: Home
    - api:home/visits: true
    - app-root-element:home/visit-listener: true
    - home-page-layout:homepage/dynamic-homepage-layout:
        config:
          customizable: true

homepage:
  defaultWidgets:
    - id: scorecard-aggregated-card
      ref: scorecard-aggregated-card
----

For the full configuration procedure and the availability status of the New Frontend System, see the {product} documentation.
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHBUGS-3970
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhbugs-3970", role="rn-done"]
TechDocs custom MkDocs plugins must be allowlisted::
+
--
With this release, TechDocs generation permits only a built-in set of MkDocs plugins, including `techdocs-core`, `search`, `material/search`, `redirects`, `group`, and `material/group`. Plugins outside that set are removed before the build, and a warning is logged. The MkDocs `markdown_extensions` configuration is also sanitized more strictly, including mapping-style declarations, so dangerous or dynamically configured entries might be stripped.

Documentation that relied on custom MkDocs plugins builds without those plugins unless they are explicitly allowlisted. Features provided by removed plugins or stripped markdown extensions no longer appear in generated documentation.

[NOTE]
====
To continue using a custom MkDocs plugin, add it to `techdocs.generator.mkdocs.dangerouslyAllowAdditionalPlugins`, or supply it through `techdocs.generator.mkdocs.defaultPlugins`. Only allowlist plugins that you trust in your documentation generation environment.
====

.Example
[source,yaml]
----
techdocs:
  generator:
    mkdocs:
      dangerouslyAllowAdditionalPlugins:
        - my-custom-plugin
----
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHBUGS-3981
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhbugs-3981", role="rn-done"]
The `dynamic-home-page` plugin is renamed to `homepage`::
+
--
Before this update, the home page plugin was named `dynamic-home-page`. With this release, the plugin is named `homepage`, and the `dynamic-home-page` name is no longer available. If your `dynamic-plugins.yaml` file references `dynamic-home-page`, update the entry to use `homepage`.
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHPLAN-239
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhplan-239", role="rn-done"]
{product} images are rebased on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10::
+
--
[IMPORTANT]
====
This is a breaking change. The {product} container images are now based on Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 10. You must migrate your existing installations to the new RHEL base version. For more information, see the {product} documentation.
====

With this release, the {product} container images are based on RHEL 10 instead of the previous RHEL base version.
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHPLAN-256
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhplan-256", role="rn-done"]
Plugin wrappers for Technology Preview plugins are removed::
+
--
This release removes the plugin wrappers for all Technology Preview plugins. The `dynamic-plugins.default.yaml` file now references some of these plugins from their `oci://ghcr.io` location instead of from the wrapper that was embedded in the `rhdh-hub-rhel9` container image.
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHPLAN-846
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhplan-846", role="rn-done"]
The New Frontend System is now the default frontend::
+
--
{product} 2.1 now runs on the Backstage New Frontend System (NFS) by default. NFS-compatible dynamic plugins provide pages and other UI through extensions.

[IMPORTANT]
====
This is a breaking change. The legacy Old Frontend System (OFS), including its Scalprum integration, is removed and cannot be re-enabled. Before you upgrade to 2.1, complete the following steps:

* Remove `APP_CONFIG_app_packageName=app-next` and `ENABLE_STANDARD_MODULE_FEDERATION=true` if you set them to enable NFS in an earlier release. NFS no longer requires these settings.
* Check custom and third-party frontend plugins for NFS support. Migrate and re-export legacy-only plugins before you upgrade. Plugins without NFS support do not appear in the application.
* Migrate frontend UI wiring under `dynamicPlugins.frontend` to the NFS `app.*` configuration, including `app.extensions` and `app.routes.bindings`. Continue to use `dynamic-plugins.yaml` to install and enable dynamic plugins.
====

For more information, see the link:https://github.com/redhat-developer/rhdh/blob/release-2.1/docs/dynamic-plugins/migrating-plugins-to-new-frontend-system.md[Migrating plugins to the New Frontend System] and link:https://github.com/redhat-developer/rhdh/blob/release-2.1/docs/dynamic-plugins/migrating-config-to-new-frontend-system.md[Migrating configuration to the New Frontend System] guides.
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHPLAN-933
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhplan-933", role="heads-up jtype-feature jstatus-in-progress rn-done"]
Authentication providers are no longer shipped statically with {product}::
+
--
[IMPORTANT]
====
This is a breaking change. Authentication providers are no longer statically shipped with {product}. You must install each provider as a dynamic plugin and configure it under `auth.providers.<id>`.
====

Guest login is no longer enabled automatically when the environment is set to `development`. To use guest login, install the Guest dynamic plugin and configure it under `auth.providers.guest`.

The `disableIdentityResolution` configuration is removed. For auxiliary providers that are used only for source control management (SCM) authentication for plugin access, omit `signIn.resolvers` instead.
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHPLAN-934
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhplan-934", role="rn-done"]
Plugin wrappers for generally available plugins are removed::
+
--
This release removes the plugin wrappers for all generally available (GA) supported plugins. The `dynamic-plugins.default.yaml` file now references some of these plugins from their `oci://ghcr.io` location instead of from the wrapper that was embedded in the `rhdh-hub-rhel9` container image.
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHPLAN-1006
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhplan-1006", role="rn-done"]
The Global Floating Action Button plugin is removed::
+
--
The `global-floating-action-button` plugin was deprecated in {product} 1.9 and is removed in this release. It is no longer included in the default dynamic plugins configuration or the Red Hat plugin catalog. To add quick actions and shortcuts, use the Global Header plugin instead, which offers similar features.

[IMPORTANT]
====
If your configuration still enables the `global-floating-action-button` plugin, remove that entry before you upgrade.
====
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHPLAN-1058
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhplan-1058", role="rn-done"]
The {product} Helm chart values are restructured::
+
--
This release restructures the {product} Helm chart values to improve the configuration experience by addressing list-merge limitations and simplifying the values schema. This restructure is not backward compatible with the previous chart.

[IMPORTANT]
====
Because the values structure has changed, you cannot pass your old values file directly to the new chart. You must migrate your values before you upgrade your existing Helm release. For full migration guidance about the fields that changed or were removed, see the link:https://github.com/redhat-developer/rhdh-chart/blob/release-2.1/charts/rhdh/docs/migration-from-backstage-chart.md[Helm chart migration guide].
====
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHPLAN-1235
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhplan-1235", role="rn-done"]
The Plugin Certification Program is removed::
+
--
This release removes the Plugin Certification Program from {product}. Certification badges are removed from the Extensions Catalog metadata, and certification fields and labels are ignored. You no longer need to maintain the `extensions.backstage.io/certified-by` annotation.
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHPLAN-1409
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhplan-1409", role="rn-done"]
Scorecard metric IDs use lowerCamelCase naming::
+
--
[IMPORTANT]
====
This is a breaking change that requires manual action. You must update your configuration to use `lowerCamelCase` for all Scorecard metric IDs to ensure compatibility.
====

Before this update, Scorecard metric IDs followed the `snake_case` naming convention. With this update, the metric IDs are changed to `lowerCamelCase` to align them with the existing `app-config.yaml` naming convention.
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHPLAN-1444
[id="removed-functionality-rhdhplan-1444", role="heads-up jtype-feature jstatus-in-progress rn-done"]
app-config ConfigMaps must contain exactly one data entry::
+
--
[IMPORTANT]
====
This is a breaking change. Existing deployments that use multi-entry app-config `ConfigMap` resources break after this update. If you have a multi-entry app-config `ConfigMap`, split it into separate single-entry `ConfigMap` resources.
====

All app-config `ConfigMap` resources, both the default and those specified in the custom resource (CR), must now contain exactly one data entry. This requirement ensures a predictable merge order, because Kubernetes does not guarantee the iteration order of `ConfigMap` data entries.
--

// https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHIDP-17464
[id="removed-functionality-rhidp-17464", role="rn-done"]
OAuth sign-in no longer uses unverified emails::
+
--
With this release, OAuth profile handling respects negative email verification information from the identity provider. If the provider marks an email as unverified, {product} no longer uses that address for identity resolution.

Users who previously signed in through an email-based OAuth sign-in resolver might fail to authenticate if their identity provider supplies an unverified email. Make sure that accounts used with {product} have verified emails at the provider, or use a sign-in resolver that does not depend on email.

[NOTE]
====
This change does not affect dedicated OIDC-based providers, such as Keycloak or Red Hat build of Keycloak (RHBK) OIDC.
====
--
